ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, promulgated November 23, 1962, as amended); Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 5927, promulgated February 5, 1999, as amended); Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (Act No. 6516, promulgated April 2, 2001, as amended); Customs Act (Act No. 1090, as amended); Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information; Financial Services Commission regulations on beneficial ownership identification; Korea Customs Service licensing rules requiring full disclosure of ultimate beneficial owners of licensed customs brokerage entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (certified extract from the commercial registration register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court of the registered seat of the LLC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issue a certified court-issued extract; authenticate by (i) Hague Apostille from the Authentication and Apostille Division of the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the using state is an Apostille Convention member, or (ii) consular legalization through the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the destination state's embassy or consulate in Seoul if the using state is not an Apostille Convention member; the two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (subsisting registration, tax clearance, and no delinquency certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service through Hometax, together with the Commercial Registration Office of the competent District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the tax clearance and registration certificates, have any private signature authenticated if required, then apply exclusively for a Hague Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention states, or apply exclusively for consular legalization through the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the destination state's consular post for non-member states; sequential chaining of Apostille and consular legalization is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the appointed customs brokerage representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of the LLC's registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The board resolution must be executed as a notarial deed before a Korean notary; the notarial deed is then authenticated either by a Hague Apostille issued by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for a destination state party to the Apostille Convention, or by consular legalization processed through the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the destination state's representative office where the destination state is not a party; the two authentication mechanisms are mutually exclusive and never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court, with notarial certification where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Take the registry-certified copy and obtain a Hague Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the recipient jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member; for non-member jurisdictions, obtain consular legalization from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the recipient jurisdiction's consular office; do not combine the two procedures in any sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and anti-money laundering clearance from a licensed Korean commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean banking institution regulated by the Financial Supervisory Service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank compliance officer signs the reference letter; if the destination requires signature authentication, have the bank officer's signature notarized before a Korean notary, then apply exclusively for a Hague Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille states or exclusively for consular legalization for non-Apostille states; parallel routes, never sequential.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence is required for every beneficial owner and natural-person officer: verify identity using a government-issued ID, the registered corporate extract, and bank-issued confirmation; screen all individuals and entities at formation and continuously against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the United States Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctions lists (including SDN and non-SDN lists), European Union and United Kingdom consolidated financial sanctions databases, the Republic of Korea Financial Intelligence Unit designated-persons notices, and the Korea Customs Service brokerage license revocation and administrative penalty registers; conduct enhanced PEP screening of domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates; adopt automated watchlist monitoring with independent false-positive adjudication, escalation to the compliance officer, and mandatory suspicious transaction reporting to KoFIU within the statutory deadline whenever money laundering, terrorist financing, trade-based money laundering, or sanctions evasion indicators appear in the beneficial ownership chain or proposed customs brokerage counterparties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: I-Net (Internet Registration Office) of the Supreme Court of Korea (www.iros.go.kr), used in conjunction with the Korea Customs Service UNIPASS broker license identifier search for customs brokerage trade-name clearance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be registered in Hangul and must end with the legal form suffix Yuhan Hoesa meaning limited liability company; a foreign-language name may be registered as a trade name in parentheses but may not replace the Hangul registered name; the four-tier naming convention requires a unique Hangul identifier, a business purpose descriptor in Korean, the statutory Yuhan Hoesa suffix, and no false indication of a Korean government body, bank, securities house, insurance company, or unlicensed customs brokerage; foreign corporate names are transliterated phonetically in the registry and the English name appears as a supplemental trade name only.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection by the commercial registration officer, the applicant may file a written reconsideration petition with the head of the competent district court registration office within 14 days, or a request for administrative adjudication with the Administrative Appeals Commission within 90 days under the Administrative Appeals Act; alternatively, an administrative litigation action may be filed with the competent district court under the Administrative Litigation Act. The appeal must include the proposed Hangul name, the registry search result, the purpose clause of the draft articles, the rejected application receipt, and proof of filing fee payment. The appeal officer must issue a written disposition addressing each stated rejection ground, and an additional name reservation or amendment may be submitted if the disputed name remains unavailable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the registered office for a Korea Customs Service licensed customs brokerage entity. The registered office must be a fixed physical place within the customs control district, evidenced by a lease agreement for at least one year, a visible door sign matching the registered Hangul corporate name, dedicated office space suitable for storing customs declarations and bonded transit records, telephone and utility connections, and availability for service of process and unannounced inspections. Korean commercial banks will reject a virtual office address when opening corporate operating accounts because the Real Name Financial Transactions Act requires in-person verification of officers and a physical business address consistent with the employment contract and tax invoice registry; local tax authorities similarly reject virtual office addresses for business registration under the Value-Added Tax Act. For a non-resident-owned LLC, the registered office must be maintained through a resident physical office manager or an authorized compliance agent in Korea, and the office must remain continuously open during ordinary business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspections are likely and must be anticipated. Checklist items: (1) exterior door sign matching the registered Hangul name and trade name; (2) original lease and security deposit documentation; (3) issuance of local tax invoices from the registered address; (4) displayed customs broker license; (5) retained import, export, customs declaration, and bonded transit records; (6) employment contracts and resident office manager records; (7) utility and internet bills; (8) Korean corporate bank account statements and real-name financial transaction records. Quantified risk: approximately 70 percent likelihood of an unannounced Korea Customs Service field inspection within the first 12 months of active licensed brokerage operations, approximately 40 percent likelihood of a National Tax Service or municipal tax office physical audit within the same period, and higher risk where the beneficial owner is non-resident, the industry is customs brokerage, or the registered office is in a high-density commercial zone.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (상법), Articles 287-2 through 287-45 (establishment of limited liability company / 유한회사), as supplemented by the Framework Act on Administrative Regulations and the Customs Act (관세법), Article 155 and Presidential Decree provisions governing customs broker licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office (등기소) under the court registration jurisdiction where the registered office is located, operating through the Korean Court Information Center (인터넷등기소) online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) together with the application for company registration (법인설립등기신청서) submitted on the court's prescribed registration form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not mandate a minimum paid-up capital for a limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa). However, for a customs brokerage license under the Customs Act, the Korea Customs Service requires the applicant legal entity to maintain adequate financial capacity, documented through a certified bank balance certificate or escrow confirmation for paid-in capital sufficient to cover estimated annual bonded transactions and liability insurance premiums, as determined by the Director General of an Regional Customs Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND SHAREHOLDERS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY), DULY ADOPTED ON [DATE] AT [TIME], AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY. PRESENT: [NAME(S)] AND [NAME(S)], BEING ALL OF THE DIRECTORS AND ALL OF THE SHAREHOLDERS OF THE COMPANY, hereby waiving formal notice in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and applicable provisions of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. IN THE MATTER OF THE ORGANIZATION OF THE COMPANY AND THE INITIATION OF ITS LICENSED BUSINESS. WHEREAS, the Company has been incorporated as a limited liability company for the purpose of conducting customs clearance brokerage, bonded transit management, and related consulting services; WHEREAS, the Company has received the requisite statutory approvals and has adopted its Articles of Incorporation; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTION: 1.1 The initial issued capital of the Company be, and hereby is, confirmed as the amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation. 1.2 Each subscriber to the shares of the Company as identified in the share subscription ledger shall make full payment of their contribution, in cash or in kind as approved, to the escrow account designated by the founders on or before the date of this Resolution, and the directors are authorized to verify the receipt of such capital and to cause the share register to be duly updated. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: 2.1 The BANK OF KOREA branch located at [Branch Address] be, and hereby is, designated as the principal bank of the Company. 2.2 Each director and the authorized signatories, namely the Representative Director and the CFO, be and hereby are authorized, any two acting jointly, to open, operate, and close bank accounts in the name of the Company, to sign checks, drafts, and electronic payment instructions, to access the Automated_Broker_Interface_ACH and wire transfer facilities, and to execute related security procedures, in all cases subject to the internal control policy of the Company and the relevant provisions of the Real Name Financial Transaction Act. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: 3.1 The registered office of the Company be, and hereby is, fixed and adopted at [Name of City/Gu/Street Address], within the Republic of Korea, and the Representative Director be authorized to execute the lease agreement, pay the security deposit, obtain the certified copy of the building registry, and to file the registration of transfer of the registered office with the respective Registry Office. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: 4.1 [Name], be, and hereby is, appointed as the Representative Director (대표이사) of the Company, with authority to manage the ordinary business affairs and to represent the Company in all matters, subject to prior resolution of the Board for extraordinary matters. 4.2 [Name], be, and hereby is, appointed as Statutory Auditor (감사) of the Company, where such appointment is required or where the Articles of Incorporation so provide, with the powers and duties prescribed under the Commercial Act. 5. NATIONAL CUSTOMS BROKER LICENSING IMPLEMENTATION: 5.1 The Representative Director be, and hereby is, authorized to prepare, sign, and submit the customs broker license application to the Korea Customs Service, including filing of the financial soundness evidence, office lease documentation, and the fidelity insurance bond, and to respond to any requests from the customs office and to execute the acceptance certificate upon grant of the license. 6. GENERAL: 6.1 Any director, officer, or agent of the Company shall be and hereby is authorized to execute any instruments, deeds, certificates, or documents, and to take any ancillary actions, as may be legally required to give full force and effect to the transactions contemplated by this Resolution. This Resolution, having been put to vote, was passed unanimously by all directors and all shareholders present and is effective immediately. RESOLVED this [DAY] day of [MONTH], [YEAR].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Screening and Search Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Regional Court Registry (intermediate internet registration service) and local municipal administrative office through Hometax / Court Net portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the incorporation filing, the applicant must conduct a name search through the Korean Court Information System to verify that the intended Korean corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered corporate name. If the name is acceptable, obtain the provisional name-preservation or clear the name search result for attachment to the registration application. Any change of name during the search period requires a restart of the process. Fees for the name search are approximately KRW 5,000 to KRW 20,000 per search.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate name search / name availability confirmation issued by the court registry information system
Passport or resident registration card copy of the founder(s)
Power of attorney if a local agent is used
Foreign investor identification documents if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, select up to three alternative names in priority order and resubmit the name search within 5 business days; the registry office will not refund the name search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public (공증인) or the head of the concerned law office exercising notarial authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean with full statutory clauses under Articles 287-2 through 287-45 of the Commercial Act. All incorporators or their duly authorized attorneys must appear before a notary public to have the Articles executed and notarized, proving the legal capacity and consent of the parties. The notarized Articles must include the corporate purpose clause covering customs brokerage and bonded transit management, share capital structure, name of directors, auditor, and registered office address. After notarization, obtain at least two certified true copies from the notary for use in registration and license applications.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Identification documents of all incorporators/directors
In-housing certificate or proof of the registered office
Notarized power of attorney if an attorney executes on behalf of any incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires amendments, counsel shall amend the non-mandatory clauses and amend the notarized document or execute a supplementary notarized amendment deed; re-notarization is completed within 2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Payment into the Corporation's Escrow Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank located in Korea (e.g., NongHyup Bank, Shinhan Bank, or KB Kookmin Bank) selected by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional escrow bank account in the name of the corporation for the purpose of capital contribution. Thereafter, each subscriber shall wire or deposit the paid-in capital amount into the escrow account and obtain a certificate of deposit (예금잔액증명서) indicating that the full amount has been received and credited to the account of the corporation on or before the statutory contribution deadline. The deposit certificate must be dated no earlier than 7 days before the court registration filing. This certificate serves as conclusive evidence of paid-up capital before the Registry Office.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application
Notarized Articles of Incorporation (copy)
Identification documents of the representative director
Company name reservation confirmation
Certificate of deposit / balance confirmation issued by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is expired or insufficient, request a renewed balance certificate from the bank on the next business day; any currency conversion or foreign-source wire holds must be resolved through the bank's AML compliance officer before the registration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Corporate Registration Application to the Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registry Office (등기과) with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing via the Korean Court E-filing system (대법원 인터넷등기소)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal application for creation of a limited liability company to the court. The application must be accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital payment certificate from the bank, the corporate name search result, and a copy of the lease agreement for the registered office. The registrar will examine whether all mandatory clauses are present and whether the officer appointments are lawful. After the application is screened, pay the registration surtax and court registration fee and receive the certificate of completion of registration (법인등기사항전부증명서). Once registration is perfected, the company may demand issuance of a corporate seal certificate and open a permanent corporate bank account with a fresh balance-certificate if the escrow balance is to be moved.
required_dossiers: Application for company registration in prescribed Form (법인설립등기신청서)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of capital deposit (balance certificate)
Certificate of registered office location (lease agreement or title deed with certified building register)
Certificate of name search / name preservation confirmation
Identification and appointment documents of directors and auditor
Power of attorney or electronic certificate if submitted online
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a correction order, the applicant must submit a written explanation and amended dossiers within 5 business days; if the registration is suspended due to unresolved capital certificate issues, obtain a fresh certificate and reinstate the application by filing a supplemental submission with a new court stamp.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs Broker License Application Filing Under the Customs Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Customs Service (관세청) and the relevant Regional Customs Office (세관장)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After corporate registration is complete, the company must file a separate application for the customs broker license (관세사 또는 통관업 허가) with the regional customs office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business. The application must prove that the company meets the customs broker eligibility requirements: a full-time licensed customs broker (관세사) employee or director, office space meeting physical standards, no disqualifying criminal or administrative record, and financial capacity evidenced by bank balances or insurance guarantees. The customs office will conduct an on-site physical inspection of the office premises and check the feasibility of the electronic data interchange system for the Automated_Broker_Interface_ACH and Korea Customs Service's electronic clearance network. Upon approval, the license is issued and the company is assigned a customs broker code for filing import/export declarations.
required_dossiers: Application for customs broker license (관세사/통관업 허가 신청서)
Corporate registration certificate (법인등기사항전부증명서)
Certificate of employment of a licensed customs broker with resume and license copy
Office lease contract and floor plan satisfying customs office location requirements
Financial soundness evidence (bank balance certificate, paid-in capital ledger, or guarantee insurance)
Certificate of no disqualifying criminal record for the representative director and licensed broker
Business plan describing customs brokerage services and bonded transit management
Consent to electronic filing / electronic data interchange system registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is withheld or returned due to incomplete documentation, the company must submit the missing or corrected documents within 14 calendar days. If the license is denied, the company may reapply after curing the deficiency or file an administrative appeal with the Korea Customs Service within 30 days of notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax Registration and Business Start Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (국세청) including local tax office; plus local district tax authority (구청/군청)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of corporate registration, the company must apply for a business registration certificate (사업자등록증) from the local district tax office. The application must include the corporate seal certificate, the registration certificate from the court, and the lease contract of the business office. After the NTS issues the business registration certificate, the company must also register for value-added tax, corporate tax, local income tax, and the electronic tax invoice system. If the company will employ workers, the workplace must also be registered with the Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service and the National Pension Service. Since the business is a customs brokerage house, no additional industrial manufacturing licensing is required; however, a business-specific license to handle cash or client funds may be required under the Anti-Money Laundering Act.
required_dossiers: Application for business registration
Certificate of corporate registration (legal entity certificate)
Corporate seal certificate
Copy of the corporate seal
Lease agreement or ownership deed for office
Customs broker license if already issued
Identification of the representative director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS indicates discrepancies in the office location or business type code, amend the business registration application and re-submit online through Hometax within 5 business days. Back-dated business registration will be issued if the amendment is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Activation and AML Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank (same bank or another Korean bank) together with the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) for AML reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the business registration certificate is obtained, the company must activate its permanent corporate bank account. The bank will conduct its own due diligence under the Real Name Financial Transaction Act and the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information. The company must provide the corporate seal certificate, legal entity registration certificate, business registration certificate, the beneficial owner declaration, and a board resolution authorizing the signatories. The bank will set up the automated broker interface ACH and wire payment rails. The company must also adopt an AML internal control policy and, within the required period, file any CTR or STR reports through the FIU system for transactions over KRW 10 million or suspicious activities respectively.
required_dossiers: Corporate legal entity registration certificate (법인 등기사항전부증명서)
Business registration certificate (사업자등록증)
Corporate seal certificate and seal (인감증명서 및 인감도장)
Copy of board resolution appointing authorized signatories
Passport or ID cards of signatories and beneficial owners
AML compliance manual and internal control policy
Power of attorney or electronic certificates for those persons opening the account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional beneficial ownership documentation, respond within 10 business days; if the account is frozen during AML review, obtain the FIU's acceptance of the STR and provide the bank written evidence of ongoing licensing and administrative compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Korea Customs Service (Korean Customs Service / 관세청) and Ministry of SMEs and Startups / Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy for any incidental bonded warehouse economic activity; site-specific municipal licensing under the respective metropolitan city or provincial government for storage if actually operated.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Broker License (통관업 허가 / 관세사 자격에 기반한 관세사사무소 등록) issued by the Regional Customs Office; supplementary Bonded Warehouse License (보세창고 운영허가) if physical bonded storage is operated.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (환경부) and the local environmental office (지방환경청)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Environmental Registration not required for an office-based customs brokerage house operating only administrative brokerage, document processing, and data transmission. If a physical bonded warehouse or any light assembly or handling of cargo beyond storage is operated, the project falls under the 'Small-scale Environmental Review' category if floor area exceeds 5,000 square meters or hazardous cargo storage is involved; for minimal storage, a non-statutory environmental self-check may suffice.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for pure administrative customs brokerage because there is no industrial discharge. If bonded warehouse operations are added: wastewater discharge must meet the Clean Water Act effluent standards of BOD less than 10 mg/L and suspended solids less than 10 mg/L for discharge to public waters; VOC emissions from trucking/diesel handling equipment must comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act and not exceed fugitive emissions limits; hazardous waste must be disposed of through a licensed waste treatment company with manifest documentation under the Waste Management Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (소방안전관리자 선임 및 소방정비 확인) issued by the Fire Defense Marshal / National Fire Agency for the occupied office if floor area exceeds 400 square meters or underground floors are used; building structural load inspection certificate (건축물대장상 구조안전확인서) from the building owner or municipal office; and occupational safety clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act requiring a safety and health management plan if more than five workers are employed; assessment of the office fire-fighting equipment and evacuation route through written confirmation issued by the district fire station.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax Service (www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign non-resident investor first files the Foreign Investment Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through KOTRA or a designated domestic bank. The Yuhan Hoesa is then incorporated at the competent Korean district court commercial registry. Within 20 days of commencing business, the company must submit a business registration application to the competent district tax office, attaching the articles of incorporation, court-issued corporate registration certificate, lease or ownership evidence for the domestic place of business, appointment of director documents, passport copies of foreign shareholders, and the Foreign Investment Report certificate. The district tax office issues the Business Registration Certificate containing a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves concurrently as the Corporate TIN, VAT registration number, and customs identifier. Because the entity is a Korean domestic corporation, it is classified as a resident taxpayer with entity-level taxation; if there is no domestic executive with a Korean address, a domestic tax manager must be appointed under the Framework Act on National Taxes to receive and file all NTS correspondence and VAT returns through HomeTax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box election, partnership pass-through classification, or hybrid mismatch entity election. A Yuhan Hoesa is per se a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax, VAT, and local income tax surcharges.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 - there is no turnover threshold for VAT registration; every business operator, including a Yuhan Hoesa, must register within 20 days of business commencement. Simplified taxpayer status is available only to individual small businesses with annual taxable turnover below KRW 30,000,000, not to a corporate entity such as this licensed customs brokerage house.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoice issuance is mandatory under the Value-Added Tax Act through the NTS HomeTax Service. Tax invoices for taxable supplies are transmitted to the HomeTax e-Tax Invoice system upon issuance, and each valid electronic tax invoice receives an NTS issuance/approval number that functions as an anti-fraud digital control. The system operates as a real-time transmission and cross-matching model rather than a pre-approval fiscal clearance model. Registered businesses may transmit via the NTS open API or use the HomeTax web interface; anti-fraud controls include public key certificate authentication, unique NTS-assigned invoice numbers, issuer/receiver cross-matching, and automatic reconciliation against VAT returns and customs export declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Value-Added Tax Act Article 21 and its Presidential Decree, exported goods are zero-rated when the goods are physically exported from Korea under an accepted Korea Customs Service export declaration, are delivered to a foreign buyer, and the exporter retains evidence of export clearance and inward repatriation of export proceeds. For services supplied by this licensed customs brokerage and bonded transit management company, zero-rating applies only where the service is supplied to a non-resident recipient, is part of the international transport or export clearance chain, and is used outside Korea; domestic customs clearance services for local importers remain standard-rated at 10%. The zero-rated supply must be reported on the VAT return, issued as an export tax invoice, and supported by the full documentary bundle. The input VAT attributable to zero-rated export supplies may be recovered through the ordinary VAT return or an early VAT refund application to the NTS.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Bill of Entry / export declaration receipt accepted by Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS system, showing the exporting business registration number and HS classification)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill for air cargo) issued in the Korean exporter's name
Commercial Invoice and export sales contract identifying the overseas buyer and the precise services or goods supplied
Packing List and cargo manifest as filed by the licensed customs broker
Licensed Customs Brokerage engagement record and broker's Customs Act filing log evidencing the export clearance mandate
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate / Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by an authorized Korean foreign exchange bank showing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Bank confirmation or foreign exchange transaction record proving repatriation of export proceeds within the statutory period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: During audit, the NTS cross-references VAT returns and e-tax invoices with Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declarations and bank foreign exchange receipts. If the mandatory export documentation and foreign exchange repatriation evidence are not produced, export proceeds are not collected within 180 days without approved extension, or the export is determined to be a fabricated or circular transaction, the zero-rating is retroactively denied, 10% VAT is reassessed on the supply value, and statutory additional taxes apply: 20% for underreporting and 40% for fraudulent or malicious non-reporting under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act, together with late-payment interest and clawback of any VAT refund already paid. Submission of a false export declaration or false electronic tax invoice also triggers criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act and customs fines/penalties under the Customs Act, including imprisonment and monetary penalties for the responsible officers and the licensed customs broker.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates an open yet prudently regulated foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current account transactions such as trade settlements, remittance of service fees, dividends from foreign investment, and ordinary customs brokerage payments. Capital account transactions, including equity injections, cross-border loans, and real estate acquisitions, are subject to prior declaration, registration, or reporting to a licensed foreign exchange bank or the Bank of Korea. There is no broad surrender requirement for export proceeds; exporters are generally permitted to retain foreign currency in licensed foreign currency accounts, although all receipts must be repatriated through a domestic foreign exchange bank and reported via the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). Profit and dividend remittance out of Korea is permitted if the original foreign investment was duly registered under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the payout is supported by audited earnings; however, the banking institution will conduct source-of-funds and tax clearance checks. In practice, authority remains concentrated in the Korean financial regulatory ecosystem, requiring a resident domestic bank relationship for any significant KRW clearing, and non-residents seeking to establish treasury operations must navigate the requirement for local corporate registration, tax registration, and a foreign investment certificate for capital verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received through a registered domestic foreign exchange bank and must be reported to the authorities via the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). The statutory collection deadline is 15 months from the date of the export declaration, unless prior approval for extension is obtained from the Foreign Exchange Administration. There is no mandatory conversion ratio for ordinary export foreign currency receipts; exporters may hold 100% of proceeds in foreign currency accounts. However, upon any conversion into KRW, the transaction must be executed at a licensed bank and coded under an approved foreign exchange purpose code.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Primary Operational KRW & USD Account / Capital Escrow Account
Primary Operational KRW & USD Account / Capital Escrow Account
Primary Operational KRW & USD Account / Capital Escrow Account
Secondary Operational KRW & USD Account / Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited to non-feasible. Non-resident fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) and virtual banking entities such as Revolut Business and Wise Business do not hold a domestic banking charter in South Korea and therefore cannot provide KRW-denominated local clearing, IBAN-equivalent KRW accounts, or access to Korean domestic payment rails (e.g., KFTC / HOFOS). They also cannot act as the primary foreign exchange bank for export proceeds surrender reporting or Foreign Investment Promotion Act capital registration. Such EMIs may be used solely as auxiliary payment gateways for trivial cross-border USD transfers outside the KRW clearing system, but all regulated treasury functions must be routed through a licensed commercial bank in Korea.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors of a foreign-owned Korean entity generally must appear physically in-branch for real-name KYC verification under the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act. In exceptional cases, remote consular proxy opening is possible if a directors' resolution appoints a local representative or attorney, accompanied by apostilled corporate documents and a power of attorney notarized at an overseas Korean consulate. However, most Tier-1 Korean commercial banks require at least one identified officer or attorney-in-fact to be physically present for in-branch telephone/SMS ARA validation, and significant treasury accounts will trigger a mandatory face-to-face compliance interview with the anti-money laundering officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity for a non-resident shareholder whose ultimate owner resides in a high-risk or tax-secrecy jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled corporate registry extract, audited organizational chain chart, certified passport copies for all beneficial owners above 10% control, beneficial ownership declaration form, and a sworn source-of-wealth statement backed by 12 months of audited bank statements from the remitting jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the declared customs brokerage license scope and onward payments to maritime or logistics counterparties in Myanmar, Iran, or other sanctioned trade corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korean Customs Service (UNI-PASS) license certificate, letters of engagement with customs clearance clients, bills of lading, airways bills, import/export declarations, customs broker indemnity insurance policy, and a counterparty AML/KYC declaration confirming the absence of sanctioned vessel or cargo exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually rapid ACH transaction volume or high-frequency foreign remittances disproportionate to the initial paid-in capital of the customs brokerage house.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Forecasted transaction schedule, existing master service agreements, proforma invoices from freight port operators, carriage contracts, and a three-year financial projection with quarterly duty payment and custody disbursement projections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of Korean economic substance, i.e., no office lease, no local payroll, or no national health insurance and employment insurance registrations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered officer's lease agreement, corporate bank account tax registration certificate, 4 Major National Insurances enrollment list, wage ledger, and a physical inspection photograph dossier signed by the foreign exchange bank manager.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound foreign direct investment must be routed through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank. The transfer must use the approved foreign exchange purpose code for equity ownership acquisition, with SWIFT MT103 stating the registered foreign investor name and investment registration number. Upon receipt, the receiving bank will issue a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate and represent the capital injection as paid-in capital under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Capital verification is completed through a bank-issued certificate of deposit plus a shareholders' resolution and statutory auditor confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements from the Korean customs brokerage entity are primarily settled via SWIFT MT103 direct transfers for freight, duty, and warehouse charges; commercial letters of credit (MT700) are used for bonded transit or consignment inventories; documentary collections are used only for completion of transactions involving title-transfer marine transit cargo. All THBW payments will be processed through Korean termination rails (KFTC) for domestic duties, with cross-border amounts subject to FEIS reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts with a genuine underlying trade invoice, up to 100% of the contracted settlement amount
Cross-currency swaps for eligible capital account operations with in-out tenor matching the foreign investment risk term

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for onshore Korean entities are legally restricted; offshore non-deliverable swaps are permissible only when a Korean enterprise hedge does not form an onshore KRW settlement obligation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and closing financial statements (including attached general balance sheet and statement of income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the immediately following fiscal year (for a December 31 year-end); for a non-calendar fiscal year, within three months from the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers a non-report surcharge equal to 20% of the tax payable; unpaid tax in excess of KRW 2 million bears delinquency interest accruing daily at the statutory rate set by the NTS (currently approximately 10.5% per annum); continued non-operation or protracted non-filing for more than six months exposes the entity to involuntary closure, suspension of business registration by the NTS, and administrative strike-off from the corporate registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual member resolution or written consent approving balance sheet, income statement and distribution of profits (if any)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate Records of the Yuhan Hoesa (on-site resolution; no filing fee or government submission unless external audit is required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of the fiscal year-end (e.g., no later than March 31 for a calendar-year entity); indefinite if waiver consented to by all members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No administrative filing penalty applies, but failure to hold or document the annual member decision causes the financial statements to be regarded as void for inter-creditor reliance; officers may be subject to a civil sanction under the Korean Commercial Act, and when combined with unapproved accounts, provides grounds for a court-ordered dissolution by a member or creditor petition.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Customs Brokerage Business Annual Activity Report and renewal/upkeep of the standing customs guarantee surety bond or cash deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Customs Service (KCS) and the competent Regional Customs Office where the brokerage license was granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by January 31 of the following year (performance and revenue data for the prior calendar year); the surety bond amount must be recalibrated and maintained at all times, with updated bond certificates filed within 10 business days of January 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual activity report or to maintain the required surety bond is an express statutory license default under the Korean Customs Act; first violation triggers suspension of the customs brokerage license for up to 15 days, and a second or persistent violation triggers revocation of the license and delisting from the Customs Brokerage Registry; an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million (approximately USD 7,400) may be assessed for unapproved business activity; continuing operations without a valid surety bond may also trigger criminal sanction and a closure order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation and (if foreign-owned) Foreign Investment Status Annual Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) for UBO AML filings; Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) for the foreign investment annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO confirmation: annually by March 31 following the fiscal year-end and within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; Foreign investment annual report: within 60 days after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., by March 1 for a December 31 year-end), and any ownership change affecting foreign investment status must be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual foreign investment report may trigger a negligence fine up to KRW 20 million (approximately USD 14,800) and loss of foreign-invested enterprise tax benefits; false or omitted UBO reporting to KoFIU is subject to administrative fines up to KRW 100 million (approximately USD 74,000) under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information, and deliberate suppression of UBO data may result in criminal prosecution and imprisonment up to three years.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (mutatis mutandis applied to a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company) and its Enforcement Decree, an independent external audit by a certified public accountant is compulsory if: (a) total assets as of the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.9 million); (b) the company is a domestic subsidiary of a listed global parent and the parent's consolidated total assets exceed KRW 12 billion; or (c) the Korea Customs Service or Financial Services Commission in writing requires an audit because of the scale of the customs brokerage bond transactions or bond-management account, ordinarily when annual bonded transit/trade settlements exceed KRW 50 billion (approximately USD 37 million). Korean external audit rules do not apply a statutory headcount trigger to LLCs; the sole quantitative triggers are asset-based and, where specially imposed, transaction-volume-based. For all mandatory audits, the balance sheet, income statement, statement of appropriation of retained earnings, and notes must be represented under K-IFRS.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS as endorsed by the Korea Accounting Standards Board (KASB) is mandated for all companies subject to external audit; private companies that do not meet audit thresholds may elect K-GAAP (General Purpose Financial Statements for SMEs) under the Korea SME Accounting Standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, any Yuhan Hoesa with non-resident ownership must file an annual foreign-investment status report to KOTRA/MOTIE within 60 days after the fiscal year-end; any transfer or issuance of equity that alters the foreign-owned percentage must be reported within 30 days of the event. For AML purposes, as a licensed customs broker, the company is a non-financial business under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information; it must obtain, verify, and maintain beneficial ownership information of its principals and must update the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) within 30 days of any change, with annual confirmation of the UBO register attached to the annual business report filed with the Korea Customs Service.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (member list of the Yuhan Hoesa)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 9,000 - USD 28,000 (if mandatory audit threshold is met; USD 0 otherwise)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive statutory base rates of 9% up to KRW 200M, 19% above KRW 200M up to KRW 20B, 21% above KRW 20B up to KRW 300B, and 24% above KRW 300B; maximum marginal headline rate is 24% before the 10% local income tax surcharge
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax credits for research and development and capital investment; temporary investment tax credit for qualified trade-facilitation facilities; free economic zone and foreign-invested enterprise income tax holidays (50% to 100% exemption for 3 to 5 years); no patent box regime exists, so effective incentives are limited to statutory credits and qualifying free-zone exemptions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Standard Return Form for Each Business Year (Form No. 401) and all required schedules filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year; calendar-year companies must file and pay by March 31 of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 - Fiscal Year Opening and Closing Dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: First and last day of the tax accounting period and the number of days in the period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Yuhan Hoesa controlled by non-residents, align the fiscal year with the foreign parent only if bona fide business reasons exist; a mismatch between the Korean entity and the parent fiscal year may trigger transfer pricing scrutiny and creates an additional reconciliation burden for intercompany customs brokerage invoices

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Total Gross Revenue and Book Net Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross customs brokerage commissions, transit management fees, ANDEC bonded warehouse handling revenue, and other operating income as reflected in the statutory accounting books, together with net income before corporate tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separate principal-agent pass-through customs duties, government clearance charges, and bonded transit duties from taxable commission revenue. A licensed customs broker must keep a written agency contract for every pass-through item; otherwise the tax authority may gross up the entire remittance as taxable revenue. Payments to a non-resident service fee account without an invoice and service evidence are treated as undeclared Korean-source income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book net income reconciled with statutory add-backs, tax-exempt income, deductible expenses, special deductions, and carried-forward losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions require valid tax invoices; amounts paid to foreign affiliates for logistics software, management consulting, and customs compliance advisory must be at arm's length and must be supported by a cost-benefit file. Unsupported outbound service fees are added back and may be recharacterized as deemed dividends where the beneficial owner is a foreign parent, creating a second withholding exposure

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculated by applying the progressive statutory brackets to taxable income, then reducing for tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply each statutory bracket only to the corresponding slice of taxable income. A non-resident-owned Yuhan Hoesa may claim foreign tax credit only for foreign taxes paid by the Korean resident legal entity on foreign-source income; it may not use credits belonging to the foreign shareholder. The foreign tax credit is subject to the per-country limitation and must be evidenced by the foreign tax assessment or officially certified receipt

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Additional Taxes and Penalty Surcharges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Underreporting surcharges, unfounded or unjust underreporting penalties, unfaithful-return surcharges, and late payment interest
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident shareholder schedule is omitted or false, the return is characterized as an unfaithful and unjust return, exposing the entity to a 40% unjust underreporting surcharge under Article 66(3) of the Corporate Tax Act. Licensed customs broker officers must separately report personal income; the corporation cannot shift taxable brokerage income into exempt personal allowances of the shareholder or nominee director

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Foreign Corporate Shareholder and Repatriation Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed schedule of foreign corporate and individual shareholders, country of tax residence, direct and indirect ownership percentages, beneficial owner chain, and actual profit distributions made to each non-resident
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the tax residency certificate and beneficial ownership declaration for every non-resident shareholder before applying treaty-computed withholding. Failure to disclose an offshore holding entity constitutes a false statement in every withholding calculation and can expose the Korean entity to secondary withholding liability, an additional 20% withholding penalty, and criminal referral for deliberate non-disclosure

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing incurs a surcharge of 20% of the unpaid tax where no valid tax invoice and books are maintained; ordinary underreporting incurs a 10% surcharge and unjust or fraudulent underreporting incurs a 40% surcharge; delinquency interest accrues at 0.022% per day. Criminal evasion involving concealment of Korean-source customs brokerage income is punishable under Article 116(1) of the Corporate Tax Act by imprisonment up to two years or a fine equal to twice the evaded tax, and the responsible director is jointly liable for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory dividend withholding tax is 20% plus a 2% local income tax surcharge, for a combined 22% withheld at source on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders; treaty-reduced rates are usually 0% to 15% depending on the DTA, shareholding threshold, and qualified resident status
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, authenticated by apostille or consular legalization where required; (2) file the non-resident corporate withholding tax treaty exemption application with the Korean paying company before the dividend, interest, or royalty is remitted; (3) provide board resolutions, the complete shareholder register, and a beneficial ownership declaration proving the recipient is not a conduit or pass-through; (4) update the documentation annually and retain it for six years. A Korean payer that applies a treaty rate without the completed application and valid Tax Residency Certificate becomes jointly liable for the unwithheld 22% plus a 20% additional withholding penalty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound royalties and interest is 20% income tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge, also a combined 22% gross rate; treaty rates generally range from 0% to 15% depending on the DTA. Royalty withholding applies to the gross royalty without allowance for underlying costs; interest withholding applies on gross paid or credited interest unless a specific interest article of the DTA reduces the rate

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File are mandatory when the total annual amount of cross-border related-party transactions with foreign related enterprises exceeds KRW 10 billion; a simplified contemporaneous transfer pricing report is sufficient where the total transaction amount is at or below KRW 5 billion; customs brokerage and freight-forwarding transactions to foreign group entities must be priced on an arm's length basis and the benchmark study must separately analyze the brokerage service margin and the customs duty valuation treatment
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea enforces a substance-over-form doctrine through anti-abuse rules in the International Tax Adjustment Act, controlled foreign company rules, and judicial disregard of artificial corporations. A customs brokerage Yuhan Hoesa claiming treaty benefits or reduced withholding must perform its core income-generating activities in Korea: licensed customs brokerage operations, economic staffing with qualified customs brokers, business premises, risk management, contract negotiation, and board decision-making. A passive non-resident-owned shell with no local substance will be treated as a conduit or sham, and the foreign beneficial owner may be treated as the taxable taxpayer

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion and False Invoice Chain
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The managing director signs a return that excludes cash or offshore-remitted brokerage commissions, inflates doubtful receivables, or records expenses supported by fictitious tax invoices from a related freight forwarding company in order to eliminate taxable profit before repatriating cash to foreign shareholders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 116(1) of the Corporate Tax Act: imprisonment up to two years or a fine equal to twice the evaded tax; Article 66(3) imposes a 40% unjust underreporting surcharge; Article 60 of the Value-Added Tax Act imposes false-tax-invoice penalties and criminal sanctions for entering a fictitious electronic tax invoice into the VAT system
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 399 of the Korean Commercial Code, a director is liable to the company and creditors for damages caused by fraudulent or grossly negligent management. Tax authorities may pierce the corporate veil and impose joint and several liability on the director for the evaded corporate tax, penalties, and interest. The director is also blacklisted as a serious delinquent taxpayer, subjected to a travel ban, asset seizure, and public disclosure, and may receive imprisonment up to two years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Shell Company and Treaty Shopping for Repatriated Profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The non-resident owner forms a Yuhan Hoesa with no substantive Korean staff, a nominee director, and no real decision-making authority, and then streams dividends, interest, or customs brokerage royalties to an offshore entity that claims a lower treaty withholding rate under a DTA despite having no genuine business activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service will deny treaty benefits under the anti-abuse provisions of the International Tax Adjustment Act, recharacterize the income as Korean-source income of the actual beneficial owner, impose 22% withholding tax plus a 20% additional withholding penalty, and order corrected withholding filings for all prior open tax years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the treaty-favorable remittance and signed the withholding declarations are jointly and severally liable for the withholding shortfall and penalties. A nominee director who merely stamped the forms is civilly liable for the misrepresentation to the tax authority, faces blacklisting and departure restrictions, and may be prosecuted as an accessory to tax fraud, carrying imprisonment up to two years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Foreign Exchange Violations in Cross-Border Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cash, wire, or ACH transfers of customs brokerage commissions and corporate profits are directed to an offshore shell account without a foreign exchange bank declaration, without beneficial ownership data, and without suspicious transaction reports to the Financial Intelligence Unit, using the licensed customs broker's Automated Broker Interface payment rails to move funds through multiple jurisdictions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The penal provisions of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act impose imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to KRW 200 million; Article 14 of the Financial Information Act requires mandatory suspicious-transaction reporting and failure to report carries administrative fines and criminal referral; trade-based money laundering can result in confiscation of the transferred property and blacklisting by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who design or approve the undisclosed remittance are personally liable for liquidated damages and repatriation costs, face civil asset seizure, travel bans, and are prohibited from serving as officers of a licensed customs brokerage. In aggravated cases, the director is prosecuted as a principal money launderer rather than a corporate representative, with imprisonment up to three years and personal forfeiture of the laundered proceeds
